name: Agama'gor
summary: Agama'gor stands north of the road from Camp Taurajo toward Mulgore. Bristleback quilboar hold this encampment in the southern Barrens, keeping pressure on the nearby Horde outpost.

sections.title: A Bristleback Stronghold
sections.body: Agama'gor is a Bristleback stronghold in the southern Barrens. Its huts, brambles, and crude totems lie close to Camp Taurajo. The quilboar threaten travelers moving between the Barrens and Mulgore’s grassy hills, and Horde scouts and hunters fight to contain them.

sections.title: Blood Shards and Exile
sections.body: Bristleback quilboar in Agama'gor carry crimson stones called Blood Shards. Mangletooth, an exiled quilboar held captive at Camp Taurajo, seeks these stones because of ancient beliefs about Agamaggan’s sacred essence. Horde adventurers raid the encampment for shards and trade them to Mangletooth for tribal charms.

faq.answer: Agama'gor is a large Bristleback quilboar settlement in the southern Barrens, directly north of the road west from Camp Taurajo toward Mulgore.

faq.q: Why are the Bristleback quilboar here so hostile?
faq.answer: Quilboar believe all land touched by the fallen Ancient boar god Agamaggan belongs to them. The Bristlebacks see the nearby tauren and orcs of Camp Taurajo as invaders on their ancestral soil.

faq.q: What can you find in Agama'gor?
faq.answer: Bristleback quilboar in Agama'gor carry Blood Shards, crystallized deposits of primal power. You can trade them to Mangletooth, an exiled quilboar in Camp Taurajo.

faq.q: Who is Mangletooth and how does he relate to this place?
faq.answer: Mangletooth is an exiled quilboar held in a cage at Camp Taurajo. He resents his kin and offers Horde adventurers protective charms in exchange for Blood Shards taken from the Bristlebacks of Agama'gor.

angles.text: As Horde defenders pass through Camp Taurajo, keeping the Bristlebacks of Agama'gor in check helps protect the outpost. Their warriors remain a priority.
As a tauren, you face danger from Agama'gor's marauders along the path to the Great Gate and Mulgore. They threaten supply lines and pilgrims.
